title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is almost entirely pictorial. It sits between a text page on tangential ('points base à l'infini') base points for a DVR, i.e. the map Π1(T_x^*) → Π1(U), and the next page, which computes explicit Belyi-type maps for 'monogones' and 'bigones': g1(z) = -(1/4)(z-1)^2/z and g2(z) = g1(z^2) = -(1/4)(z-1/z)^2. It reads as a working sheet on the combinatorics of the 2-dimensional level of the genus-0 Teichmüller tower, i.e. M_{0,5} or its configuration of base points and paths.

(1) Heading 'pentagones orientés' with an ink dodecahedron. Its edges carry two series of letters, a–e on visible faces and a'–e' on hidden faces. That gives 10 symbols on 30 edges, so each symbol would appear 3 times. Dots sit at edge midpoints, and a rotation arrow marks the orientation of a pentagon. A word b'e'd'e' (or b'c'd'e') is written beside it, probably a path or relation read around a face.
- The count 10 × 3 = 30 matches the real locus of M̄_{0,5}. That locus is tiled by 12 pentagons, the associahedra K_4, indexed by dihedral orders of 5 real points. Each of the 10 boundary lines D_ij(R) ≅ RP^1 is cut into 3 edges by the 3 divisors D_kl disjoint from it.
- But a genuine dodecahedron has 20 vertices of valence 3, while M̄_{0,5}(R) has 15 vertices of valence 4. So the dodecahedron is either a different model or a combinatorial device for orienting and labelling the 12 pentagons. One candidate is the classical 5-colouring of dodecahedron edges, where each face sees all 5 colours and gets an induced orientation. This links to A5 ≅ icosahedral group acting on 5 labels.

(2) Spheres labelled D_0, D_01, D_1, D_12, D_2.
- D_0: marked points all on an equator, with an arrow giving a cyclic orientation and a sign +.
- D_1: some points on the equator and others on meridians through the poles, with '(+↺)'.
- D_2: a pole point, equatorial points and meridians, with signs + and −.
- D_01 and D_12: intermediate pictures, one with a point marked x.

The most natural reading is a stratification of genus-0 configurations by type of reflection symmetry (real structure):
- D_k: the configuration is fixed by an antiholomorphic involution permuting k conjugate pairs and fixing the remaining points on the real circle. For 5 points, k = 0, 1, 2 gives 5, 3 or 1 real points.
- D_01, D_12: the incidence or transition loci between adjacent strata.
The signs ± would be orientations of the real circle or of the resulting cells. In modern terms this is a cell or 'Lego' description of the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,5} with respect to tangential or real base points. It feeds the pentagon relation of the Teichmüller groupoid.

(3) A small shaded triangle, perhaps a simplex orientation convention.

(4) A second ink dodecahedron with edges labelled only by a–e, with dots and crosses.

(5) A large pencil net of pentagons labelled a–e, with curved arrows giving the orientation of each face. This is an attempt to check by unfolding that the face orientations induced by the labelling are coherent or alternate.

(6) Three pencil spheres with polar caps, meridians and points on the equatorial band. These are configurations with dihedral symmetry about a polar axis, like those that give the monogon/bigon covers on the next page.

Overall purpose: build a combinatorial (cellular, oriented) model of the second level of the genus-0 Teichmüller tower, compatible with the base-point formalism being developed. The precise referents of the labels cannot be read off the page.
errors: No explicit claims are written down, so nothing can be checked strictly.

If the dodecahedron is meant as a cell model of M̄_{0,5}(R), the counts do not match. The dodecahedron has 20 trivalent vertices; M̄_{0,5}(R) has 15 four-valent vertices, χ = -3, and is non-orientable (#5 RP^2). It can at best be a covering or auxiliary combinatorial model.
The orientation arrows in the pencil net seem to have been corrected (dashed arrow, overwritten letters 'c', 'b', 'd'). This suggests the first coherence attempt failed or was revised.

ideas.what: Dodecahedron with edges labelled by letters and an induced orientation of each pentagonal face ('pentagones orientés'), checked on an unfolded net
ideas.modern_name: 5-colouring of dodecahedron edges / A5 symmetry; pentagonal cells of the real locus of M̄_{0,5} (associahedra K_4)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Kepler/Klein for icosahedral symmetry); Kapranov and Devadoss for associahedral tilings of M̄_{0,n}(R) (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,5} and the pentagon relation in the Teichmüller tower, but not, to my knowledge, this dodecahedral picture

ideas.what: Strata D_0, D_1, D_2 (and transitions D_01, D_12) of genus-0 point configurations, by number of conjugate pairs under a reflection of the sphere, with orientation signs
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of M_{0,n} by real structures (types of antiholomorphic involutions); real loci of M_{0,n} for twisted real structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Real moduli of pointed genus-0 curves with arbitrary involutions: Ceyhan (2007); Kapranov, Devadoss, Etingof–Henriques–Kamnitzer–Rains for the totally real case
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to cell decompositions of modular multiplicities and the use of real points; exact correspondence unsure

ideas.what: Spheres with polar caps and meridians: symmetric configurations, tied to tangential base points at the poles and the monogon/bigon covers of the next page
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points and dihedral-symmetric dessins (Belyi maps of 'monogones' and 'bigones')
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (dessins d'enfants, Teichmüller tower, base points)

missed.claim: An attempt to build an oriented cellular (pentagonal/dodecahedral) model of the 2-dimensional level of the genus-0 Teichmüller tower. The cells are indexed by real-structure types D_0, D_1, D_2 and their incidences D_01, D_12, with labelled edges and coherent face orientations. Using all real structures, not just the totally real one, to cellularize M_{0,5} differs from the later Lego literature, which works with pants decompositions and the totally real locus.
missed.quote: pentagones orientés ... b'e'd'e' ... D_0 ... D_01 ... D_1 ... D_12 ... D_2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A cell structure on M_{0,5} mixing several real forms could give an alternative presentation of the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid and its pentagon relation, with base points at symmetric configurations. That is relevant to Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory and to real moduli spaces (Ceyhan, Devadoss, Etingof et al.). The page itself is too fragmentary to state a result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page appears to show Grothendieck stratifying 5-point genus-0 configurations by real-structure type and organizing pentagonal cells with oriented labelled edges on a dodecahedral model. This is a suggestive unpublished detail of how he pictured M_{0,5} in the Teichmüller tower. But it is purely pictorial, its exact meaning is uncertain, and related structures (associahedral tiling, pentagon relation, real moduli) are well known.
transcription_corrections: Heading reads 'pentagones orientés' (handwriting abbreviated, roughly 'pentagons orient-').
The word beside the first dodecahedron could be 'b'c'd'e'' rather than 'b'e'd'e''; the second letter is ambiguous.
Beside D_1 there is a crossed-out sign before '(+↺)'.
Beside D_2 the signs are '+' at the top and '−' at the bottom, with a crossed-out mark between.
D_0 is written as a stylized 'D' with subscript 0, not 'D_b'.
The edges of the first dodecahedron carry dots at edge midpoints (marked points on edges), not only labels.
